To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a single small molecule, (-)epi­gallo­catechin­-3-gallat­e (EGCG), can inhibit the formation and remold the structure of prions (infectious amy­loid forms) of the yeast prion pro­tein Sup35.

a small molecule antagonist of prion formation can select for novel amyloid polymorphisms and that combining two small molecules synergistically antagonizes prions without selecting for drug-resistant prions.

a single small molecule drug can select for drug-resistant prion strains and that a minimal drug cocktail, a small set of drugs, can antagonize all prion strains without selecting for drug-resistant prions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of therapeutic agents that target protein-misfounding processes and their application in the treatment of neurodegenerative disease.
the development of therapeutic strategies for prion diseases and other protein misfolding diseases.
the development of therapeutic strategies to combat protein-misfolds and their associated diseases.

the combination of EGCG and 4,5- bis-(4-methyoxyanilino) phthalimide is an effective and synergistic combination of drugs that can be used in the treatment of neurodegenerative conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single small molecule drug is not enough to antagonize the complete spectrum of misfolded protein forms that cause neurodegenerative disease.
we have shown that a single small molecule, EGCG, is able to antagonize the formation and even remodel preformed prions.
we discovered a novel mechanism for drug resistance in prion disease and that a minimal drug cocktail can be used to antagonize the complete spectrum of amyloid polymorphisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of minimal cocktails of drugs to treat amyloid diseases might be more effective than using single drugs.
a single drug can be effective in treating a particular neurodegenerative disease, but the disease can become drug resistant.
the amyloid polymorph problem must be addressed to develop effective therapies for amyloid-related diseases.
